transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen, David Park, Lena Ortiz, Samir Gupta (HarborBridge)
Link to deck: short/harborbridge-renewal-deck (shared)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in focused on: 1) capacity scaleout for Q3 (headroom for marketing spike), 2) APAC edge activation timeline and lead times, 3) data residency / KMS questions for contract extension. Customer requested updated pricing tiers and an E2E benchmark.

Agenda / Topics covered:
- Current usage baseline and ramp forecast
- Hosted vs Dedicated capacity tradeoffs for predictable latency
- APAC edge (private VPC vs hosted region) provisioning timelines
- Security: KMS, audit logs, retention, SOC 2 alignment
- Next steps and timing for contract amendment

Action items (recorded in call body as well): Jordan to send pricing + lead times; Priya to run benchmarks; Carlos to send compliance docs; HarborBridge to confirm SLOs and endpoint list.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving out time. Agenda's up front, quick sync — renewal horizon coming up, we want to align on capacity and APAC edge provisioning. Priya and Carlos from our side are here. Maya, do you want to kick off with where you are on capacity needs?
[00:23] Maya: Sure, yeah thanks. So our Q3 marketing push plus a new partner integration in August means we expect a sudden RPS bump, roughly a 2.8x delta on our chat generation traffic. Current host is US-west and eu-west, so we need APAC coverage. Main asks: predictable p99 latency < 350ms for APAC users, and data must remain in APAC region for a subset of requests.
[00:45] Priya: Got it. When you say subset, is that a routing rule in your app or at the request level? Like do you tag requests?
[00:52] Maya: It's per-tenant flag. Partner data flagged "apac-sov" needs to stay within APAC and must be encrypted with our KMS.
[01:02] Jordan: Thanks. Quick clar — renewal term and uplift: you're evaluating either a Dedicated pool reservation for predictable throughput or adding more hosted capacity with routing rules. Which direction is the finance/team leaning?
[01:16] David: Finance is open but operations want predictability. Dedicated looks interesting but the main blocker is lead time — how long to provision APAC dedicated nodes? And also, what’s cost delta vs hosted?
[01:28] Priya: Provisioning dedicated capacity in APAC typically takes 3-5 weeks depending on GPU mix and cluster schedule; we can do burst capacity earlier via hosted region while Dedicated is being staged. Cost delta — ballpark is 30-45% premium for a reserved dedicated pool compared to pure pay-as-you-go hosted, but you get steadier p99 and capacity guarantees. We can run an optimized quantization profile to reduce token cost, that usually helps unit economics.
[01:55] Samir: Are those numbers for A100 or H100? Our model is currently running a 7B quantized variant, so it's lighter — we mainly care about memory for KV caches during long conversations.
[02:08] Priya: For a 7B optimized path we'd advise a 4096-token KV strategy and on H100 the latency is lower; A100 will still meet p99 in many cases but H100 gives more headroom. We also have continuous batching knobs to keep CPU overhead down.
[02:24] Lena: From security side, we need to clarify the KMS integration model — customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed — and the form of audit logs we'll get. Also retention windows and the ability to run on-prem for sensitive tenants.
[02:38] Carlos: Sure, we have both options. Customer-managed KMS is supported via our KMS connector (we've done AWS KMS and Cloud HSM). For audit logs, we can deliver per-request metadata with timestamp, model id, route id, and a hashed prompt/response pointer. We'll share a sample schema. On-prem deployments are part of the Private offering; that is a separate contract but we can pilot scoped tenants.
[02:59] Maya: Ok, good. Can you share the sample audit log format today or after the call?
[03:05] Carlos: I'll upload to the shared folder post-call.
[03:09] Jordan: Let's talk risk and fallback — say Dedicated APAC is delayed. How do you recommend we keep traffic within SLOs?
[03:18] Priya: Short answer: staged approach. 1) Immediately route APAC traffic to hosted APAC region (live in days), 2) enable prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token compute, 3) once Dedicated is ready, move tenants over with canary rollout. We also recommend setting a fallback policy to an EU edge during failures. Canaries can be per-tenant.
[03:41] David: On prefix caching — is that transparent to our app or do we need to change how we maintain session state?
[03:48] Priya: Mostly transparent. We support automatic KV caching that persists between calls if the session id is passed in; you'd need to pass the session identifier. There's also an optional explicit cache control header if you want finer control.
[03:58] Samir: Any effects on model consistency? Like do we see split-brain with caching?
[04:03] Priya: Not usually. KV cache is ephemeral, keyed by session; if you switch backends we'll warm the KV as the session continues. For strict determinism we'd recommend pinned model versions and warming runs.
[04:14] Maya: Can you quantify costs for the caching / burst strategy? Our CFO asked for the delta between immediate hosted ramp vs dedicated reservation.
[04:22] Jordan: We'll send an updated pricing model but rough guidance: short-term hosted burst with caching is cheaper up-front but your per-token run-rate rises with sustained traffic. Dedicated saves on per-token costs over committed monthly usage. We'll include a modeled scenario for the 2.8x spike showing 30/60/90 day impact.
[04:40] Lena: On compliance — SOC2 and ISO snapshots will be helpful. Also need to know how audit logs are stored and if we can push copies to our S3 in APAC.
[04:50] Carlos: We can stream audit logs to your S3 bucket in APAC or we can provide a secure pull endpoint. We'll include retention TTL options and an encryption-at-rest schema.
[05:01] David: About contract amendment: if we commit to a 12-month Dedicated pool, what happens if usage drops? Is there a flex-down clause?
[05:10] Jordan: We have a typical reserved commitment with quarterly checkpoints. We can build a flex-window into the amendment — e.g., up to one tier down after a 60-day notice with adjusted pricing. We'll have legal draft language once you indicate the tier.
[05:22] Maya: Good. For timelines — we need APAC live by Aug 15 ideally. Is that feasible?
[05:28] Priya: Tough but possible. If you accept hosted APAC (fast path) + staged Dedicated, we can have hosted edges live in 3-7 days, and Dedicated pool in APAC in ~3-5 weeks. That would meet Aug 15 with a Dedicated ramp up if we start immediately.
[05:42] Samir: Benchmarks — we want p50/p95/p99, cold-start and warm-start for session flows. Are you able to do that with our traffic pattern?
[05:50] Priya: Yes, we'll need a token/sample corpus and endpoints list. We'll mirror your workload shape in the benchmark and run throughput tests. Expect a 4-hour window for a representative run.
[06:00] David: We'll provide sample payloads and a token distribution by Friday.
[06:04] Jordan: Great. A couple of open items — data residency: are you good with KMS customer-managed and audit log streaming to your APAC S3?
[06:12] Lena: Yes, that's our preference. Also we need encryption certs for in-transit and at-rest details for contract review.
[06:18] Carlos: We'll include TLS cipher suite details and the at-rest envelope encryption diagram in the docs.
[06:24] Maya: One more ask — can we have a dedicated Redwood SE as a point for the first two weeks of the pilot? We want someone to help with rollout and troubleshooting.
[06:32] Jordan: Absolutely, Priya can be primary and we can allocate another SE for nights/weekend on-call during the go-live window.
[06:38] Priya: Happy to. We'll put a rotating on-call schedule in the runbook.
[06:42] [Small cross-talk, doc link posted to chat]
[07:05] Jordan: Okay let's recap so we all have the same expectations. Action items: Jordan sends pricing and APAC lead times; Priya schedules benchmark; Carlos uploads SOC2/ISO and KMS connector docs; HarborBridge provides sample payloads, token distribution, SLO targets, and endpoint list. Target dates included in action items. Any other blockers?
[07:26] Maya: One potential blocker — partners legal wants to review the amended data processing addendum for APAC. Can you confirm turnaround time?
[07:33] Jordan: Legal turnaround typically 3-7 business days after we get counters and scope. We can escalate for a faster review if needed.
[07:40] Lena: Also please confirm whether audit logs will include hashed prompt pointers only (we can't allow raw prompts for compliance).
[07:47] Carlos: Yes, we can set the default to hashed pointers; raw data transfer is opt-in and would require a separate agreement.
[07:54] David: One last thing — competition. We've had outbound from MegaInference and CloudAI offering cheaper per-token. Why would we stick with Redwood?
[08:03] Jordan: Two reasons — predictability and operational tooling. Our Dedicated offering + Console gives per-token and per-route cost breakdowns and easy rollouts. Also we have guardrails and fallback policies which reduce customer impact during capacity events. We'll put a comparative note in the pricing doc.
[08:17] Maya: That helps. Ok, I'm comfortable moving forward pending the docs and benchmark. Let's tentatively aim to sign amendment by July 23 if benchmarks go well.
[08:26] Jordan: Sounds good. We'll target the next call after benchmarks for final alignment.
[08:30] Carlos: I'll share the uploads by tomorrow.
[08:33] Priya: I'll reach out to schedule the benchmark window and send prerequisites.
[08:36] Meeting end 

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard tokens: "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, "dedict" for Dedicated, minor punctuation issues. Speaker labels mostly correct.

Recorded attachments referenced: shared/harborbridge-renewal-deck.pdf, shared/harborbridge-benchmark-specs.xlsx, shared/soc2-snapshot.pdf
